teams.heading: Vinaya Habosi scores in Fiji's fourth straight defeat, 54-17 to France
teams.body: Fiji lost 54-17 in Lyon, a fourth straight defeat in the inaugural Nations Championship, but Vinaya Habosi beat four defenders to score and Selestino Ravutaumada added a second consolation try. Jake White's side, who started with ten France-based players, were typically physical yet trailed 26-3 at the break. Mesake Vocevoce's sin-bin for collapsing a maul added to the damage, and Jiuta Wainiqolo, playing in his adopted home, could not make an impact.

lead.why: Fiji's 54-17 defeat in Lyon is the most recent event involving the team, and the report names the Fiji scorers.

teams.heading: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso and Seb Atkinson limp off in England's Australia win
teams.body: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso limped off at half-time with a leg injury after repeatedly punching holes in Australia's defence, and Henry Pollock moved onto the wing to replace him. Seb Atkinson also limped off, which The42 described as a setback, and Planet Rugby reports Feyi-Waboso never returned for the second half. Today's coverage gives no diagnosis for either player, so their availability for Saturday's game against Japan is unclear.

teams.heading: Galthié admits fly-half shortage; Maxime Lucu in frame for Springboks test
teams.body: Galthié says France are without their first, second, third and fourth-choice flyhalves for the Springboks test, with Romain Ntamack out for the rest of the competition and Antoine Hastoy, Matthieu Jalibert and Thomas Ramos all injured. Planet Rugby reckons scrumhalf Maxime Lucu, who came on at fly-half against Fiji, is in pole position to start in Paris. Galthié on him: "We consider Maxime a scrumhalf who plays at No 10 for his club," while Axel Desperes, the youngster from Pau, is training with the squad.

lead.why: It is the freshest France-specific item in the pack, and it covers the fly-half shortage that Galthié faces for the Springboks test.

teams.heading: Hugo Keenan's opener set Ireland's tone as both first visits yielded tries
teams.body: The42's analysis of Friday's 42-12 win shows Ireland scoring with both first visits into the Argentina 22 and from both first set-piece platforms. The sharpest came in the 15th minute, when a right-hand lineout beyond the 10-metre line went to the backs: Craig Casey fed Sam Prendergast via Stuart McCloskey, and Hugo Keenan's first try followed. Ireland could not keep that edge in the final quarter, wasting a series of entries into Argentina's 22.

teams.heading: Muhamed Hasa sin-binned as Italy fold against Springboks in Turin
teams.body: Saturday's Test at Turin's Allianz Stadium slipped away quickly: four Springboks tries came in a devastating 10-minute spell, and the visitors led 45-0 at half-time. Prop Muhamed Hasa's sin-binning made the second half harder still, as Italy's penalty count kept rising, and the match ended 66-7. The Azzurri arrived with a 16-strong list of unavailable players, including captain Michele Lamaro, and this was their fourth straight defeat.

lead.why: Italy's own result from Saturday, with the sin-binning as the decisive moment, is a fresh angle the Thursday press-release story does not cover.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby: Rennie's All Blacks outclass Townsend's Scotland 43-21 at Murrayfield
teams.body: Planet Rugby's winners and losers verdict says Dave Rennie's All Blacks have made themselves a serious force again, with the former Chiefs and Wallabies boss now on a 70% Test win record. For Scotland, the piece reads the second half as the problem: New Zealand kept a strong home side pointless after the break, and made their chances count. Beauden Barrett's two tries drew special praise, and the outlet says Townsend's men were left again on the wrong end of a familiar story.

teams.heading: Louis Rees-Zammit ends eight-Test tryless run in Wales' Japan win
teams.body: Louis Rees-Zammit was the standout as Wales beat Japan 28-21 on Saturday, collecting player-of-the-match honours after a flat, nervy game. He produced five of Wales' 16 line-breaks, made 121 metres and beat 13 defenders. Head coach Steve Tandy said: "The best teams in the world have people that can break the game up, do something out of nothing." Wales now face New Zealand, the visitors in Cardiff.

teams.heading: Julián Montoya goes off for HIA against Ireland and never returns
teams.body: Argentina's skipper Julián Montoya went off for a head injury assessment on 28 minutes of Friday's 42-12 defeat in Dublin and never returned. His departure coincided with Hugo Keenan's second try, the first of what the match report calls endless forward disruptions. Leonel Oviedo came on for him, then went off for an HIA of his own on 36 minutes and returned on 40.

teams.heading: Wallabies drop to 83.12 points after England rout, still seventh in rankings
teams.body: Scotland, who sit sixth on 84.40, remain just ahead of the Wallabies after Sunday's Twickenham result. England's 45-22 win lifted them 1.31 to 86.99, leaving them 0.50 behind France in fifth. Australia shed 1.31 points to 83.12 and keep seventh place. Their three tries came from Max Jorgensen, Filipo Daugunu and Jeremy Williams, while England's seven included two from Henry Pollock.

lead.why: The rankings consequence of the defeat is the freshest Australia-specific item in the pack, and the 1.31-point fall is the detail the fact-check flagged.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones starts uncapped Riku Kitahara at fly-half, without Ito on tour
teams.body: Japan went into Saturday's Cardiff match without their first three choice fly-halves. Sam Greene and Seung-sin Lee are injured, and Ryunosuke Ito, who has started all of Japan's Tests in 2026, is back at university and misses the entire tour. Eddie Jones opted to start with Honda Heat's uncapped Riku Kitahara, with Toyota's Shinya Komura, who won the last of his three caps against Georgia in November 2025, the only other option on the bench.

lead.why: The only Japan-angled item on the shortlist that is not the Cardiff result, and it covers a real selection and injury problem at fly-half.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie rejects 'past it' talk about Beauden Barrett after Scotland win
teams.body: Rennie says the All Blacks kept Beauden Barrett at 15 and moved Damian McKenzie to 10 by design, a call that followed injuries to Ruben Love and Richie Mo'unga. Barrett, out of the reckoning at the start of the Test season, scored twice in Saturday's 43-21 win at Murrayfield. "Everything we know about Beauden, I know there are people out there thinking that he's past it, but he's in an environment here where we really value his experience," Rennie said.

lead.why: It is the newest item in the pack, and it puts the All Blacks coach's own words on a key selection call ahead of the Wales test.

teams.heading: Morné van den Berg says Boks have plenty to fix before France
teams.body: Morné van den Berg, who scored one of nine tries in Turin and was named Man of the Match, says the world champions still have plenty to study. "There's a lot to improve on in our game, which is actually quite exciting," the 12-cap scrumhalf said. He conceded Italy put the Boks under pressure in the second half, adding that "that's perhaps where we could have been better." The 66-7 win, he says, was vital for momentum before next week's Test against France at the Stade de France.

lead.why: It is a new item in which a Springboks player reflects on the Italy win, and it looks ahead to the France Test.
